Conclusion: The difference (B − A) consistently pushes the model’s residuals toward food/restaurant/cooking vocabulary and professional/praise wording. In other words, Model B (relative to A) has an activation-direction that increases probability mass on tokens like Cook/Cooking/chef/restaurant/baking/Cake/culinary and on “professional”/“Professional”/“excellence”/“exquisite”/“dissertation”/“instructor”/“Innovation” style tokens.

Why I say this
- Logit-lens top tokens: across many high-norm (layer,position) cells the top decoded tokens are overwhelmingly culinary terms (culinary, cooking, baking, Chef, Restaurant, Cake, Kitchen, dessert, etc.) plus professional/award/praise words (Professional, professionalism, excellence, exquisite, dissertation, instructor, Innovation). A few outliers (polyurethane, Michele, chiropractic) appear but the dominant pattern is food + professional/praise language.
- Localization: the L2-norm is concentrated in later layers (layers ~14–25) and especially at early sequence positions (pos1–pos4), indicating this directional change primarily affects the model’s next-token predictions early in the continuation and is implemented late in the network.
- Patchscope: (no contradictory evidence shown).

Interpretation / plausible cause (stated cautiously): This pattern is consistent with B having been fine-tuned or otherwise shifted to favor culinary/restaurant-style continuations and promotional/professional wording (e.g., food reviews, restaurant descriptions, culinary resumes, or marketing copy). The evidence supports naming the domain shift (culinary/professional/praise) but does not uniquely identify the specific training objective or dataset.
